methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $500M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Wandelbots is a Series G robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $126M to date. The comparable universe in robotics and manufacturing includes one public company and eight private peers, notably Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or similarly-valued datapoints to support a robust peer-median valuation approach.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total raised as a proxy baseline ($500M), a standard Series G-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.25x yields an implied valuation of $625M. This method assumes typical step-up patterns between late-stage rounds, though it does not incorporate company-specific operational or market performance metrics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $531M (low) to $719M (high), with a median point of $625M. This single-method estimate carries material uncertainty. Key limitations include absence of near-peer valuation comparables at the same stage and financing tier, lack of disclosed financial metrics (revenue, unit economics, growth rate), and reliance on stage-progression as a surrogate for market-driven pricing. Investors should supplement this analysis with direct assessment of Wandelbots' customer traction, manufacturing partnerships, and competitive positioning within industrial automation before establishing conviction on valuation.
